```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

dendromatic is the computational core behind the DendroMatic applications:
cleaning and normalization of point-dendrometer time series. This vignette
walks the standard path from a raw-ish series to a cleaned one on the shipped
synthetic dataset.

```{r setup}
library(dendromatic)
```

## The example data

`dendro_sample` holds two synthetic hourly series over two growing seasons.
`SYN_Pa002` carries the two artefacts this package exists to fix: a +35 µm
sensor-reinstallation step (2022-06-15) and a multi-day data gap.

```{r raw-plot}
d <- subset(dendro_sample, series == "SYN_Pa002")
plot(d$ts, d$value, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "stem radius (µm)",
     main = "SYN_Pa002, raw")
abline(v = as.POSIXct("2022-06-15 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"), col = "red", lty = 2)
```

## Cleaning in one call

`dm_clean_series()` applies, in order: break leveling, dormancy erasure,
season alignment, and per-series zero re-basing. Break windows are passed as a
named list, one `c(start, end)` pair per break. `rerun_proc_L2 = FALSE` keeps
this vignette independent of the GitHub-only 'treenetproc' package; in a real
pipeline leave it `TRUE` so TWD and zero-growth columns are recomputed.

```{r clean}
brks <- list(SYN_Pa002 = list(
  c("2022-06-15 10:00:00", "2022-06-15 14:00:00")
))

cleaned <- dm_clean_series(
  df            = dendro_sample,
  brks          = brks,
  grow_start_dm = "01-05",   # growing season: 1 May ...
  grow_end_dm   = "31-10",   # ... to 31 October
  rerun_proc_L2 = FALSE
)
```

```{r clean-plot}
cd <- subset(cleaned, series == "SYN_Pa002")
plot(cd$ts, cd$value, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "stem radius (µm)",
     main = "SYN_Pa002, cleaned")
```

The step is gone, the dormancy period between the seasons is erased, season
two starts at season one's maximum, and the series minimum sits at zero.

## Daily predawn / midday extrema

Downstream water-relations work usually needs the daily predawn minimum and
midday maximum of tree water deficit (TWD). With a `twd` column (normally from
the treenetproc L2 step), `dm_pdmd_extrema()` extracts both in local time:

```{r pdmd}
## toy TWD: running max minus value, per series
cleaned$twd <- ave(cleaned$value, cleaned$series, FUN = function(v) {
  m <- cummax(ifelse(is.na(v), -Inf, v)); ifelse(is.na(v), NA, m - v)
})
pdmd <- dm_pdmd_extrema(cleaned, pd_start_hr = 3, pd_end_hr = 6,
                        md_start_hr = 12, md_end_hr = 15, tz = "Etc/GMT-1")
head(pdmd)
```

## Progress reporting

All engines signal progress via 'progressr' (alongside a terminal text bar).
In scripts:

```{r progressr, eval = FALSE}
progressr::with_progress(
  cleaned <- dm_clean_series(dendro_sample, brks = brks)
)
```

In a Shiny app, wrap the same call with
`progressr::withProgressShiny()` -- the core stays UI-free.

## Original names

Every function also answers to its original DendroMatic name
(`apply_breaks_and_shift()`, `raw_to_L0()`, ...), so existing scripts keep
running unchanged. See the README API map.
